edges.relation: Both split gravity into exact local work and cached distant summaries.
Both treat approximation scale as a first-class control knob.
The sweep queue provides the candidate pairs that trigger reversible micro-steps.
Round-trip error decides when encounter mode must engage or back off.
Projection thresholds and weights can be tuned against teacher trajectories.
Projection strength and softening both depend on what scales are visibly resolved.
The same gradient path supports both simulator tuning and parameter fitting from trajectories.
Calibration objectives can include reversibility and trust metrics, not only position mismatch.
Planar patches make angular broad phases especially cheap and accurate.
Patch-local exact forces pair naturally with a global near/far force split.
Patch boundaries and migrations become natural events for refreshing cached distant summaries.
Round-trip spikes can reveal when far-field caches have gone stale.
Fitted masses define new invariant targets that the projector can preserve.
Inference must account for representation-scale blur if the fitted model is to generalize across zoom levels.

bridge_chains.summary: Computational geometry narrows candidate events, event-driven integration resolves them, verification measures trust, differentiable tuning improves the engine, and inverse fitting turns the result into an exploratory lab.
Astrophysical force decomposition meets event-driven caching, then game-style world streaming, then graphics-inspired representation-aware smoothing.
Graphics-style stabilization flows into scale-aware smoothing, then lands back in a concrete astrophysical force engine.
